headline: Mistakes are information—signals showing where your model of reality doesn't match reality
universal_truth: Errors are teachers, not enemies; mistakes reveal what success hides
fun_facts: Thomas Edison conducted 1,000 failed experiments before creating the light bulb—each taught him something
Post-mortems at learning organizations study failures more than successes
Hospitals that openly discuss errors have significantly lower error rates than those that hide them
discussion_questions: How do you respond to mistakes—hide them or analyze them?
What has failure taught you that success couldn't?
How do you create safety for mistakes to be learning opportunities?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A mistake is a gap between what you expected and what happened. That gap is pure information—showing where your understanding was wrong. Mistakes aren't failures; they're data. The only real failure is not learning from them.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We fear mistakes, yet they're often more educational than successes. Why are errors such powerful teachers?

options.text: Mistakes reveal hidden flaws—success can happen for wrong reasons, but failure exposes exactly where your understanding is incomplete; errors are precise feedback
options.response: Yes. Success confirms nothing—you might have been lucky. Failure points precisely at what's wrong. Mistakes are specific, targeted information about gaps in your model.

options.text: Mistakes just show what doesn't work
options.response: True, but more specifically, they show why it doesn't work—which is actionable information...

q1.title: Success Hides Information
q1.script: When things work, you don't know why. Success confirms but doesn't explain. Failure demands explanation—forcing you to understand. Mistakes make you smarter in ways success can't.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Success Hides Information"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Analysis Required
q2.script: Mistakes only teach if you study them. Quick shame and moving on wastes the lesson. Post-mortems, reflection, and analysis extract the learning that mistakes offer.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Error Culture
q3.script: Environments that punish mistakes get hidden mistakes, not fewer mistakes. Environments that analyze mistakes openly get learning. Your relationship with error determines your learning rate.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Errors are teachers, not enemies. Mistakes reveal what success hides. Study your failures.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 287. Tomorrow, we'll explore information that helps you improve—feedback. Until then, consider what a recent mistake taught you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Mistake Analysis - What Did Failure Teach?
growTrack.activity: Think of a recent mistake or failure. What gap did it reveal between your expectations and reality? What specific lesson can you extract? How will you apply that learning going forward?
